questions.question: In an HXX designation, what does first-X code 1 mean?
questions.explanation: A first X of 1 means cold worked only, with no anneal.

questions.question: In an HXX designation, what does first-X code 2 mean?
questions.explanation: A first X of 2 means cold worked plus partial anneal.

questions.question: In an HXX designation, what does first-X code 3 mean?
questions.explanation: A first X of 3 means cold worked plus stabilized.

questions.question: In an HXX designation, what does first-X code 4 mean?
questions.explanation: A first X of 4 means cold worked plus baked.

questions.question: In an HXX designation, what degree of strain hardening does second-X code 2 represent?
questions.explanation: A second X of 2 represents quarter hard.

questions.question: In an HXX designation, what degree of strain hardening does second-X code 4 represent?
questions.explanation: A second X of 4 represents half hard.

questions.question: In an HXX designation, what degree of strain hardening does second-X code 6 represent?
questions.explanation: A second X of 6 represents three-quarter hard.

questions.question: In an HXX designation, what degree of strain hardening does second-X code 8 represent?
questions.explanation: A second X of 8 represents fully hard.

questions.question: In an HXX designation, what degree of strain hardening does second-X code 9 represent?
questions.explanation: A second X of 9 represents extra hard.
